description:
Hi! I’m a Mechanical Engineering undergraduate from India with a strong background in physics, thermodynamics, system modeling, and analytical problem-solving.

At AetherOne, I bring technical system design, data interpretation, and clear pitch structuring to turn NASA open data into a practical, scientifically valid solution for space mission design game.
summary:
Delta-V: Mission Architect is an interactive, browser-based space mission design simulation game where players step into the role of a NASA systems engineer to plan, build, and execute deep-space missions under realistic physical and budgetary constraints.
Addressing the Space Mission Design Game challenge, our application bridges the gap between overly complex aerospace simulators and oversimplified arcade games. Players select real mission targets—such as lunar polar landings or Europa flybys—and configure propulsion systems, thermal protection, power arrays, and scientific payloads while balancing strict mass, power, and delta-V budgets. Mission outcomes are driven by real NASA open datasets, including JPL Horizons orbital mechanics, planetary radiation profiles, and atmospheric entry parameters.
This project is important because it transforms real spaceflight engineering trade-offs into an accessible, hands-on learning experience. By letting students, educators, and space enthusiasts test why real NASA missions succeed or fail—such as sacrificing payload mass for extra fuel or surviving extreme thermal loads—Delta-V: Mission Architect inspires STEM literacy and demonstrates the real-world complexity of modern space exploration.
